context:
Goal: the work goes on now, and you can overrule any coordinator pick.
In plain words: when your account runs in 'overage' (over its normal use), Claude remembers a session's earlier conversation for only 5 minutes instead of an hour. A session that waits on CI longer than 5 minutes then pays to re-read its whole conversation when it wakes. The CI wait cap is how long a session waits before it checks in.
Problem (goal): the coordinator left the wait cap alone for overage, because no hook can tell when overage is on, so a second, shorter cap has nothing to switch it. The cost of that gap is unmeasured on the Mac and the PC.
Based on (notes): coordinator message, 12:17 CST Nov 12; the retrospective's audit 13:19 CST found the pick sound.
Departs from: main has no such pick on record — the work it governs follows this pick.

options.gain: No hook can tell when overage is on, so a second cap has nothing to switch on.
options.how: When the account runs in overage, the prompt cache lasts 5 minutes, not an hour; the CI wait cap does not change for it, and the gap stays recorded.
options.label: Keep the pick (Recommended)
options.lose: The other route is not taken unless you choose b.

options.gain: The other route, if you prefer it.
options.how: Add a second 300 s cap used while overage shows; no hook can read overage yet, so that reader comes first.
options.label: Overrule it
options.lose: The governed work is redone or waits for the change.

reply: You said the tradeoff was not well written; the item now says in plain words what overage does and what the cap is. In short: a leaves the wait cap alone and records the gap (no way to detect overage yet, cost unmeasured); b adds a second 300 s cap that is used only while overage shows, which needs a reader for overage first. Say b in the thread or on the page to overrule.
short: CI wait cap: leave the 5-minute overage cache as a known gap
title: CI wait cap: leave the 5-minute overage cache as a known gap
why: A coordinator pick you could not see before.
